packageRules.description: Group all non-major updates into one weekly PR
Group all major updates into one monthly PR
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Security patches get immediate PRs, auto-merge

A library's Cargo.toml floors are a promise to consumers, so in-range updates move only Cargo.lock. Cargo.lock may then need a newer Rust than the MSRV: that's fine, because the MSRV CI job resolves afresh like a consumer on the MSRV (see docs/dependency-updates.md).
dist generates this workflow and its plan job fails if it drifts from what dist would generate. Its actions move when `cargo-dist-version` is bumped and `dist generate` re-run.

The MSRV CI job pins the oldest toolchain we support on purpose; bumping it would stop checking the MSRV at all. Move it by hand together with rust-version in Cargo.toml (see docs/dependency-updates.md).
The SMB benchmark harness is excluded from the workspace because sspi pins digest =0.11.0-rc.5, which conflicts with digest 0.11.2. Independent bumps there can never resolve.

Hold GitHub's Ubuntu runner below 26.04 while that image is a public preview (actions/runner-images#14226, still preview on 2026-11-03). The Homebrew publish job runs only at release time and no PR CI exercises it, so a preview image's instability or queueing would surface mid-release. Lift this rule once #14226 is closed and the 26.04 image is GA.

Lock file maintenance (a weekly plain `cargo update`) runs only for the fuzz harness, and never automerges: Cmdr's weekly upgrades pass merges it once every version in it is at least three days old and the harness builds. It's its own workspace, so the main grouped PR never touches its lockfile, and its indirect deps otherwise drift until a release. Everywhere else it stays off: Renovate can't apply minimumReleaseAge to it (see docs/dependency-updates.md). Both paths are negated because matchFileNames also tests each package file's lockfiles.
